extracted.intended_audience: Users of TikZ/PGF (LaTeX/TeX users) creating graphics and paths
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and options for constructing, modifying, and performing actions on TikZ/PGF paths (to/node/edge operations, scoping, drawing, filling, shading, arrow tips, patterns, opacity, bounding boxes). Intended for authors writing TikZ picture code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nodes on to
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to add nodes to the paths constructed by a to operation by specifying the nodes between the to keyword and the coordinate; e.g. (a) to node {x} (b) typically behaves like (a) -- node {x} (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nodes between to and the coordinate to add labels to 'to' paths. Example: \draw (0,0) to node [sloped,above] {x} (3,2); Also works with curved to operations like to[out=90,in=180]. Note that within the to-path expansion nodes are inserted with an implicit pos option.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every to
rubrics_metrics.description: The style 'every to' is installed at the beginning of every to. By default it is set to draw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can set \tikzstyle{every to}=[draw,dashed] (or similar) to change appearance of all to paths. This style is applied automatically at the start of each to path.

rubrics_metrics.name: to path option and macros (\tikztostart, \tikztotarget, \tikztonodes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'to path' option defines the actual path inserted whenever a to operation is used. Inside the path the macros \tikztostart, \tikztotarget, and \tikztonodes reference the from-coordinate, to-coordinate, and nodes between the to and the coordinate, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default to path is '-- (\tikztotarget) \tikztonodes', so (a) to (b) expands to (a) -- (b). You can redefine to path to draw curves, e.g. to path={.. controls +(1,0) and +(1,0) .. (\tikztotarget) \tikztonodes}. It is not allowed to write '-- \tikztonodes (\tikztotarget)' because TikZ forbids a macro after '--' that expands to a node.

rubrics_metrics.name: execute at begin to / executed at end to
rubrics_metrics.description: 'execute at begin to' executes code prior to the to; 'executed at end to' executes code after the to path has been added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These options let you perform computations or draw additional paths before or after the main to path. Use them for extra effects tied to the to operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping operation ({ and })
rubrics_metrics.description: Braces ({, }) open or close scopes when encountered where a path operation is expected; options that can be applied 'locally' are scoped inside the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformations like [xshift=1cm] inside a scope only apply within that scope. Some options (e.g. color=red) do not take effect inside a scope since they apply to the path as a whole rather than local path components; be careful which options are local vs global.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node and edge operations in paths
rubrics_metrics.description: The node operation adds a node to a path but does not change the current path; it is 'external' to the path. The edge operation similarly adds something after the main path and behaves like to (it adds a to path after the main path).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nodes do not alter the geometry of the path; they attach content at points on the path. Because of their special status they are described separately (Section 13). Use edge when you want a to-like addition after the main path has been drawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: pgfextra operation (\pgfextra ... or \pgfextra ... \endpgfextra)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \pgfextra{code} inside a TikZ path to suspend path construction and TikZ's parsing, run arbitrary TeX code, then resume parsing. Alternative syntax \pgfextra code \endpgfextra is available when code doesn't start with a brace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an expert feature intended for deep macro work; should only be used by real experts inside clever macros, not on normal paths. Example: change a dimension mid-path to affect subsequent coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions on paths: draw/fill/filldraw/pattern/shade/shadedraw/clip/use as bounding box
rubrics_metrics.description: A constructed path can be drawn (stroked), filled, used for clipping, used as the picture extent, or combinations thereof. Special-purpose commands (\draw, \fill, \filldraw, \pattern, \shade, \shadedraw, \clip, \useasboundingbox) are abbreviations for \path with the appropriate options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \draw is shorthand for \path[draw], \fill for \path[fill], \filldraw for \path[fill,draw], etc. Options encountered anywhere on the path indicate actions to perform (options accumulate). E.g. \path (0,0) circle (1cm); does nothing unless draw/fill/etc present; \path[draw] (0,0) circle (1cm); draws it.

rubrics_metrics.name: color= option
rubrics_metrics.description: color=color name sets the color used for fill, drawing, and text inside the current scope (overrules special settings for fill/draw).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can omit 'color=' and give 'red!20' etc; TikZ will try unknown options as color names. For plain TeX users only gray and rgb are supported; \definecolor and \colorlet are available in limited emulation. Use draw= and fill= when you want to set drawing or filling colors separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: draw= option
rubrics_metrics.description: draw=color causes the path to be drawn (stroked) using the given color; if color omitted the last color set by color= is used. draw=none disables drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options that influence line appearance (line width, dash patterns, arrow tips, etc.) only take effect if the path is being drawn (i.e., draw set directly or via \draw). Setting draw=color on a scope sets the default drawing color for paths inside that environment but doesn't force drawing unless draw option is present on a path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line width and preset styles
rubrics_metrics.description: line width=dimension specifies the thickness of drawn lines (default 0.4pt). Predefined styles (ultra thin, very thin, thin, semithick, thick, very thick, ultra thick) set common widths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may either set exact dimensions or use style names like 'very thick'. Remember that 'style=' prefix can be omitted when applying these presets: \draw[ultra thin] ...

rubrics_metrics.name: cap option (line end style)
rubrics_metrics.description: cap=type specifies how lines end; permissible types are round, rect, and butt (default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose cap to control end appearance of thick lines. Examples illustrated with line width=10pt; use white stroke to overlay for demonstration if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: join option (line join style)
rubrics_metrics.description: join=type specifies how line joins are rendered; permissible types are round, bevel, and miter (default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select join depending on the corner appearance you want for thick polylines. Use miter with appropriate miter limit or select bevel/round to avoid long spikes at sharp angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: miter limit
rubrics_metrics.description: miter limit=factor: when using miter joins and a corner is very sharp, if the miter would protrude more than 'factor' times the line width it is replaced by a bevel join (default 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase miter limit if you want to keep miter joins for sharper angles; decrease to force bevel sooner. Examples show different visual effects with miter limit values.

rubrics_metrics.name: dash pattern and dash phase
rubrics_metrics.description: dash pattern=dash pattern sets dash/on-off sequence (metafont syntax). dash phase=phase shifts the start of the dash pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can specify sequences like 'on 2pt off 3pt on 4pt off 4pt'. Predefined styles (solid, dotted, densely dotted, dashed, densely dashed, loosely dashed, etc.) provide convenient shorthands. Use dash phase to align dashes across segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: draw opacity and opacity presets
rubrics_metrics.description: draw opacity=value sets how transparent drawn lines are (1 = opaque, 0 = invisible). 'opacity' sets both drawing and filling opacities. Several style presets (transparent, ultra nearly transparent, nearly opaque, opaque, etc.) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: draw opacity only affects stroked lines; use fill opacity for fills. Note that some PostScript output and older GhostScript versions may not support these transparency features properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrow tips (arrows= and shorthand)
rubrics_metrics.description: arrows=start-end sets arrow tips at the start and end of a drawn path (e.g., ->). Any option containing a '-' is interpreted as an arrow specification; many predefined arrow tip kinds are available and can be combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One arrow tip possible at each end; for multi-segment paths only the last segment receives arrow tips. The special arrow tip '>' is undefined by default and can be redefined with the >= option to choose a preferred default arrow style (e.g., >=latex, >=to, >=stealth). The pgflibraryarrows provides many tip shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: >= option (redefining > arrow tip)
rubrics_metrics.description: >=end arrow kind redefines the meaning of the special arrow tip '>' (and related shorthands), choosing which arrow tip kind '>' expands to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use >=to to get TeX's arrow, >=latex for LaTeX's arrow, >=stealth for pstricks-like arrow, etc. Redefining also controls swapped and doubled variants (e.g., <<, >>, |<, >|).

rubrics_metrics.name: shorten >= and shorten <=
rubrics_metrics.description: shorten >==dimension and shorten <==dimension shorten the path at the end or start by the given amount. This is useful to compensate for arrow tips or to avoid endpoints protruding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if no arrow tip is specified, you can shorten ends to adjust where the drawn stroke stops relative to specified coordinates. Often used together with thick lines or arrow tips to fine-tune endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: double option and double distance
rubrics_metrics.description: double=core color causes the path to be drawn twice: first with normal drawing color, then again with the core color (normally white) and a reduced width, producing the appearance of a double line or a bordered line. double distance sets spacing/thickness of the second drawing and selects double mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use double to create bordered lines or outlined effects. double distance controls apparent spacing (default 0.6pt). The first drawing thickness equals twice the normal line width plus the double distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: fill= option
rubrics_metrics.description: fill=color causes the path to be filled with the selected color; unclosed parts are closed if necessary. For self-intersecting or multiple closed areas, interior is determined by the chosen rule (nonzero or even odd). Setting fill=none disables filling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using fill together with draw (or \filldraw), the path is filled first and then drawn (stroked) so a filled+drawn area is slightly larger due to pen thickness. Use fill for solid shapes and combine with draw for outlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: pattern and pattern color
rubrics_metrics.description: pattern=name fills a path with a tiling pattern; patterns are either inherently colored or form-only (use pattern color to set their color).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns are not enabled by default; you need to load libraries (e.g., pgflibrarypatterns) to get predefined patterns. Form-only patterns take the current pattern color; inherently colored patterns ignore pattern color. Patterns cannot be resized/oriented without defining a new pattern; for complex cases you may simulate patterns with nested \foreach but patterns are faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior rules: nonzero rule vs even odd rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Two methods decide which points are inside a filled path: nonzero rule (default) counts signed crossings with a ray and point is inside if counter is nonzero; even odd rule counts crossings mod 2 and point is inside if number of crossings is odd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nonzero rule is more flexible; even odd rule is more intuitive for 'drilling holes' into paths. Choose even odd rule when wanting simple hole behavior (e.g., donut shapes). Examples in the manual show crossing counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: fill opacity
rubrics_metrics.description: fill opacity=value sets the opacity/transparency of fillings; it also applies to text and images inside the filled region. Separate from draw opacity; 'opacity' sets both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want translucent fills (e.g., overlapping colored circles). PostScript output may require recent GhostScript for proper transparency support.

rubrics_metrics.name: shade option and shading types (shading=axis, radial, ball)
rubrics_metrics.description: shade fills a path using the currently selected shading. shading=name selects the shading type; predefined types include axis (default top-to-bottom transition), radial (center-to-border), and ball (sphere-like highlight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If shading type doesn't naturally map to arbitrary shapes, predefined shadings render a large rectangle and then clip to the path. Use shading=ball for spherical look, shading=axis for a three-line gradient, shading=radial for circular gradients. Choose shading before applying shade or use shading= option.

rubrics_metrics.name: shading angle
rubrics_metrics.description: shading angle=degrees rotates the shading (not the path) by the given angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate an axis shading by 90 degrees to convert top-to-bottom into left-to-right, for example. This option only affects orientation of the shading's color sweep.

rubrics_metrics.name: shading color options (top/bottom/middle/left/right/inner/outer/ball color)
rubrics_metrics.description: Options such as top color=, bottom color=, middle color= set the colors used in axis shadings; left/right set axis shading with rotation; inner/outer set colors for radial shadings; ball color sets the base color for ball shadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing top or bottom color automatically selects shade and shading=axis and computes the middle color as needed (order matters: specify middle color last if giving top and bottom). inner/outer trigger radial shading, ball color triggers shading=ball. ball color never appears entirely uniform—highlights and borders mix white/black.

rubrics_metrics.name: use as bounding box (\useasboundingbox / use as bounding box option)
rubrics_metrics.description: use as bounding box sets the bounding box of the picture to the path where the option is applied; subsequent paths are ignored when computing picture size unless they enlarge it previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to control whitespace around a picture or to allow a tikzpicture to overlap main text without changing layout. Equivalent to \path[use as bounding box]. Note effect inside a scope lasts only until scope end. It simulates clipping for bounding-box purposes without actual clipping.

rubrics_metrics.name: current bounding box node
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a predefined node with rectangle shape whose size is the current bounding box; it allows you to query or use the picture's bounding box dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this node when you need coordinates or sizes relative to the computed bounding box (e.g., positioning labels at corners or computing dimensions dynamically).
